 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:37686  MFA No. 2351 of 2016  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 02.01.2016 in M.V.C.No.4886/2014 passed by the M.A.C.T., Bengaluru (SCCH-14) ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 31.10.2014 at about 08:00 pm, the husband of 1st petitioner, father of 2nd petitioner by name Thimmaiah, the deceased, while riding his TVS-XL moped bearing Reg.No.KA- 42/R-4453 hit by a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AC- 1440 killing him at the spot.
The petitioners being the dependants of the deceased have approached the Tribunal for compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after NC: 2023:KHC:37686 taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, awarded a sum of Rs.12,75,000/- with 9% interest p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Sridhar. D.S, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. O. Mahesh,
learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was aged 38 years and he was a Mestri by profession, earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has considered the income at Rs.8,000/- per month for the accident of the year 2014.
Hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation by taking the income at Rs.20,000/- per month.
Per contra learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that there is no proof that the deceased was a Mestri and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Since there is no proof of income,
the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.8,000/- and followed all the principles of assessment of compensation and awarded Rs.12,75,000/-, but the rate of interest awarded at 9% is on the higher side and it has to be reduced and there is no need for enhancement of compensation.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

2 8.
There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident and death of the deceased on account of the accident, petitioners being the dependents of the deceased entitled to claim compensation.
The material on record did point out NC: 2023:KHC:37686 that that the time of accident, the deceased was aged 45 years and the applicable multiplier is '14'.
This has been correctly applied by the Tribunal.
The deceased has no proof of income and he falls within the age band of 40 to 50 years and hence, future prospects has to be taken at 25% instead of 30% assessed by the Tribunal.
There are 2 dependants of the deceased.
Hence, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

8.1. In a case of this nature, principles of assessment of compensation is settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd.
-vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2.

sentences.text: By applying these principles, compensation has to be assessed.
In the year 2014, the income of a person with no proof of income has to be taken at Rs.8,500/- instead of (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:37686 Rs.8,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.

If all these factors are reconsidered, the assessment of loss of dependency will be Rs.8,500/- + Rs.2,125/-
(25%) = Rs.10,625/- - Rs.3,541/- (1/3rd) = Rs.7,084/- x 12 x '14' multiplier = Rs.11,90,112/-.
Under conventional heads, towards loss of consortium to wife, loss of love and affection to 2nd petitioner, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each has to be assessed.

Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate,
Rs.15,000/- each has to be assessed.
If all these are summed up, it comes to Rs.13,00,112/- as against Rs.12,75,000/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.25,112/-.
9. As rightly contended by learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the enhancement is less than 5%, the appeal has to be dismissed.

However, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, it is not proper to dismiss the claim petition as the contention of the Insurance Company regarding NC: 2023:KHC:37686 age of the deceased, future prospects and deduction towards personal expenses are considered.
Hence, it is a fit case to award global compensation of Rs.25,000/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:

ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.

iii) Petitioners are entitled to enhanced global compensation of Rs.25,000/-
with interest of 6% p.a.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
